report:
## Verdict: REJECT (a changed docstring and doc page claim a SHOW behind a leading comment is always classified as introspection, and the code does not do that)

The change is not ready to merge: the withholding logic and every acceptance criterion check out, but the `is_introspection_query` docstring and the read-only-safety doc page, both edited by this change, promise a `SHOW` exception to the fail-open rule that the code keeps only when the statement parses.
Rule applied: self-contradicting-diff carve-out → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

- VC-4: FAIL (important) — is_introspection_query returns True for a statement whose leading keyword is SHOW after any leading comments, and does so before any parse (so a SHOW statement that does not parse still classifies as introspection). [docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md:67]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The SHOW check at src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:130 is `first_sql_keyword(sql) == 'SHOW'`. first_sql_keyword (lines 41-52) only strips whitespace and leading '(' and takes the first whitespace token. It does not strip `--` or `/* */` comments, so `/* c */ SHOW TABLES` yields '/*' and `-- c\nSHOW TABLES` yields '--'. Neither matches 'SHOW' before the parse. A SHOW behind a leading comment is caught only after sqlglot.parse_one succeeds, at lines 144-149 (the code comment says 'A SHOW behind a leading comment slips past the first-keyword check'). If the parse raises, the except at lines 134-141 returns False, and if the parse returns None, line 142-143 returns False. So a comment-led SHOW that does not parse is classified as a data query. That contradicts the authored text in the claim and in docs read-only-safety.md:67 and :73 ('after any leading comments', 'a SHOW-leading statement, which returns True before any parse'). The no-comment SHOW case does return True before parsing, so the claim holds only without a leading comment. The rejections lines concern dialect and components_to_markdown and do not cover this. The doc says the guard can be disabled and the string has already executed, so an engine-valid SHOW that sqlglot cannot parse is plausible.

  </details>

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor

1. src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py lines 110-128 (the `is_introspection_query` docstring) and docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md lines 67 and 73: the text says a statement whose first keyword is `SHOW`, leading comments aside, is introspection, and that fail-open applies "apart from a `SHOW`". The code checks `SHOW` before parsing only when it is the very first token: `first_sql_keyword` does not skip comments. A comment-led `SHOW` is recognized only after `sqlglot.parse_one` succeeds, so when the parse raises, the function returns `False`. Checked at this head: with the project's installed sqlglot, `/* c */ SHOW 'abc` raises `TokenError` under mysql, postgres, sqlite and no dialect, and ``/* c */ SHOW TABLES FROM `x`` raises it under mysql and sqlite; `is_introspection_query` returns `False` for both. Either narrow the text to a `SHOW` that is the first token (or one that parses), or make the pre-parse check skip leading comments. (raised by 1/4 agents) [self-contradicting-diff carve-out] <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=not-held limb-one=not-evaluated limb-two=not-evaluated; evidence: the finding disputes which inputs the classifier counts as introspection (a functional-coverage gap) -->
2. src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py lines 134-143: the fail-open parse failure is logged only at DEBUG, and the `parsed is None` branch logs nothing. Since this change, that path also decides whether a catalog result reaches the user, and the server's default log level is `info`, so a catalog result shown because of a parse failure leaves no trace at the default level. (raised by 1/4 agents)
3. src/sqllens/tools/_format.py lines 427-428 and 478-480: `last_sql_is_introspection` is a cached value of the classifier for `last_sql`, kept correct only because two separate `if is_run_sql` branches about fifty lines apart update the flag and `last_sql` respectively. Correct at this head; moving either update would let the two drift apart with no test catching it. (raised by 1/4 agents)
4. tests/unit/test_format.py line 1936: the comment says the controls below pass without a dialect and hold on the code before this change, but `test_unparseable_sql_result_still_shown_with_dialect` and `test_chart_after_introspection_card_is_kept` pass `dialect=`, which the base `components_to_blocks` does not accept, and the chart test's expected blocks would also differ on base. (raised by 1/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: a test-file comment; no mechanism under discussion; git grep —no-index of the head view for "Controls below pass without a dialect" prints only tests/unit/test_format.py:1936; the test file is not published -->
5. docs/internal/setup/config-loading.md line 33 (not changed by this diff, already stale at base): it says `show_details` is consumed by the agent factory, which "unlocks `UI_FEATURE_SHOW_TOOL_ARGUMENTS` for the static default user group only", but `build_agent` admits the default group whatever `show_details` is. This change now relies on that card always being emitted, so a maintainer following this doc could re-gate it and start showing catalog results. The same stale reasoning remains in docs/internal/agent/factory.md line 132. (raised by 1/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: the doc sentence describes factory behavior, and making it true changes no output; git grep —no-index of the head view for the sentence prints only docs/internal/setup/config-loading.md:33; internal doc page, not published -->
6. src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py lines 23-25 and 110-113: one blank line, not two, separates the new module-level `logger` from `class UnsafeSqlError`, and the `is_introspection_query` docstring breaks mid-sentence. Not caught by the configured ruff rules. (raised by 1/4 agents)

- VC-30: FAIL (suggestion) — The comment asserts that the tests below it pass without a dialect and so hold on the code before #301. [tests/unit/test_format.py:1936]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  tests/unit/test_format.py:1936 says controls below pass without a dialect and hold on pre-#301 code. But test_unparseable_sql_result_still_shown_with_dialect (1960-1964) and test_chart_after_introspection_card_is_kept (1967-1976) call components_to_blocks(..., dialect=...). Base components_to_blocks (view-base src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:251-253) takes only `components`, so both would raise TypeError on base code. The chart test also passes dialect="postgres". Only the first three controls (1939-1957) are dialect-free. The comment is therefore wrong for two of the tests it covers. Rejections do not cover this.

  </details>

checklist.claim: is_introspection_query returns True for a statement whose leading keyword is SHOW after any leading comments, and does so before any parse (so a SHOW statement that does not parse still classifies as introspection).
checklist.source_excerpt: A statement whose leading keyword, after any leading comments, is `SHOW`
checklist.verify_hint: Check the SHOW detection in is_introspection_query: how it strips leading `--` line comments and `/* */` block comments and leading whitespace, and that it runs before the sqlglot parse and its fail-open except
checklist.evidence: The SHOW check at src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:130 is `first_sql_keyword(sql) == 'SHOW'`. first_sql_keyword (lines 41-52) only strips whitespace and leading '(' and takes the first whitespace token. It does not strip `--` or `/* */` comments, so `/* c */ SHOW TABLES` yields '/*' and `-- c\nSHOW TABLES` yields '--'. Neither matches 'SHOW' before the parse. A SHOW behind a leading comment is caught only after sqlglot.parse_one succeeds, at lines 144-149 (the code comment says 'A SHOW behind a leading comment slips past the first-keyword check'). If the parse raises, the except at lines 134-141 returns False, and if the parse returns None, line 142-143 returns False. So a comment-led SHOW that does not parse is classified as a data query. That contradicts the authored text in the claim and in docs read-only-safety.md:67 and :73 ('after any leading comments', 'a SHOW-leading statement, which returns True before any parse'). The no-comment SHOW case does return True before parsing, so the claim holds only without a leading comment. The rejections lines concern dialect and components_to_markdown and do not cover this. The doc says the guard can be disabled and the string has already executed, so an engine-valid SHOW that sqlglot cannot parse is plausible.

checklist.evidence: tests/unit/test_format.py:1936 says controls below pass without a dialect and hold on pre-#301 code. But test_unparseable_sql_result_still_shown_with_dialect (1960-1964) and test_chart_after_introspection_card_is_kept (1967-1976) call components_to_blocks(..., dialect=...). Base components_to_blocks (view-base src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:251-253) takes only `components`, so both would raise TypeError on base code. The chart test also passes dialect="postgres". Only the first three controls (1939-1957) are dialect-free. The comment is therefore wrong for two of the tests it covers. Rejections do not cover this.
